title: CRA (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) checklist for llull — VC-COM-33
status: draft 2026-10-28; obligations quoted from the EUR-Lex text (R10, R11); whether and from when each applies to llull is for counsel
applicabilityQuestions: Is llull a product with digital elements made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity today (public repository, pilots), or only from the first sale? (recital 18; FUNCTIONAL_SPEC §11 Q3)
Main establishment in Belgium: which CSIRT is designated as coordinator for Art 14(7)? (expected CCB, to verify)
Is llull outside Annex III and Annex IV (no CAD category found), so that module A internal control (Art 32(1)(a)) is available?
Is an update check enabled by default 'applicable' (Annex I Part I (2)(c)) for software whose directive is offline-first?

keyDates.what: Art 14 reporting obligations apply, also to products placed on the market before 2027-12-11
Regulation applies in full; products placed earlier are covered only if substantially modified afterwards

items.obligation: support period reflects expected use time, at least five years unless use is shorter; rationale in technical documentation
each security update stays available at least 10 years after issue or the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer

items.ref: Art 13(8) last subpara; Annex I Part II (5)
items.obligation: coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy put in place and enforced
for substantially modified successive versions, vulnerability handling (Annex I Part II (2)) may be limited to the last version if earlier users get it free of charge
if historical versions are archived publicly, users are clearly informed of the risks of unsupported software
technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market
conformity assessment (internal control, module A, if not Annex III/IV)
EU declaration of conformity and CE marking
technical documentation and declaration kept at least 10 years after placing on the market or for the support period, whichever is longer
type, batch or serial number or other element allowing identification
items.llull: version + commit in About and `llull version --json`

items.obligation: actively exploited vulnerability: early warning <= 24 h, notification <= 72 h, final report <= 14 days after a corrective measure, via the single reporting platform
severe incident affecting product security: early warning <= 24 h, notification <= 72 h, final report within one month of the notification
inform impacted users of the vulnerability / incident and mitigations, where appropriate in a machine-readable format
no known exploitable vulnerabilities at release
items.llull: dependency audit in release:check (npm, cargo, Python)

items.obligation: secure by default configuration, with reset to original state
items.llull: loopback-only backend, per-launch token (DEPLOYMENT §3); import_code off by default; FR-COM-36 reset

items.obligation: vulnerabilities addressable by security updates, where applicable automatic and on by default with opt-out, notification of updates, option to postpone
items.llull: FR-COM-15; default is an owner/counsel decision

items.obligation: protection from unauthorised access; report possible unauthorised access
items.llull: bearer token, origin / Host allowlists, CSRF guard, rate limits (server/src/security.ts)

items.obligation: confidentiality and integrity of stored / processed data; report corruptions
items.llull: pack 04 DSF (integrity, recovery); licence state HMAC; signed releases

items.obligation: data minimisation
items.llull: FR-COM-04 hashed fingerprint; FR-COM-17 redacted bundle; no telemetry

items.obligation: availability of essential functions incl. after an incident; minimise impact on other services
items.llull: read-only fallback never blocks data access (FR-COM-03); loopback-only

items.obligation: limit attack surfaces; exploitation mitigation
items.llull: risk-assessment.md (Electron hardening, sidecars, Python bridge, DWG converter as separate process)

items.obligation: record and monitor relevant internal security activity, with a user opt-out
items.llull: local security log (backend auth refusals, licence events) — to specify

items.obligation: users can securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently
identify and document vulnerabilities and components; SBOM in a commonly used machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies
remediate without delay incl. security updates; separate security updates from functionality updates where technically feasible
effective and regular security tests and reviews
items.llull: security review per release (existing /security-review skill + dependency audit + fuzz `llull fuzz`)

items.obligation: publicly disclose fixed vulnerabilities once an update is available (description, affected product, impact, severity, remediation)
facilitate sharing of vulnerability information incl. third-party components; contact address
mechanisms to securely distribute updates; automatic where applicable for security updates
security updates disseminated without delay, free of charge, with advisory messages
items.llull: FR-COM-14/15; EULA must not charge for security updates

items.obligation: manufacturer name and contacts; single point of contact for vulnerabilities and CVD policy location; product identification

(4) intended purpose, security environment, essential functionalities, security properties; (5) foreseeable circumstances leading to significant cybersecurity risks; (6) address of the EU declaration of conformity where applicable; (7) type of technical security support and end-date of the support period; (8)(a)-(e) instructions for secure commissioning and use, effect of changes on data security, how to install security updates, secure decommissioning and data removal, how to turn off the default automatic installation of security updates; (9) where the SBOM can be accessed, if made available
items.llull: FR-COM-35; docs/compliance/cra/annex-ii-user-information.md; note: (8)(e) presupposes the Annex I Part I (2)(c) default — counsel question on 'where applicable'
